resultJson.description: Stop the review loop from silently discarding sub-threshold reviewer findings. Verified against the repo: filterByConfidence (flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/ReviewLoop.scala:331) deletes issues below the flat confidenceThreshold (default 0.7) before display, leaving no trace in events, IgnoredIssues, or the progress log, and the loop then prints "No review comments" (ReviewLoop.scala:549-550). confidence is an undocumented Double on ReviewIssue; no prompt defines it. Per the reporter's decisions: (1) gate on severity × confidence and route gated-out findings into the existing IgnoredIssues channel, (3) report termination honestly, (2) define the confidence contract in the prompts/schema, (6) de-anchor reviewers from the plan, (4) prompt-only hardening of reviewer selection (no code-side content triggers, to avoid overfitting), (5) whole-PR review pass explicitly skipped.

tasks.title: Replace the flat confidence threshold with a severity-aware gate
tasks.description:
In flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/, introduce a `ConfidenceGate` value with per-severity minimum confidences and use it in `ReviewFixLoop.filterByConfidence` (ReviewLoop.scala:331-334) in place of the flat comparison.

- New small file (plain case class, no `derives` needed since it is config, not serialized): `ConfidenceGate(critical: Double, warning: Double, info: Double)` with `def admits(issue: ReviewIssue): Boolean` selecting the minimum by `issue.severity`. Scaladoc: rationale is that severity and confidence are orthogonal — a Warning at 0.55 should not share a bar with an Info at 0.55.
- Default `ConfidenceGate.default = ConfidenceGate(critical = 0.5, warning = 0.6, info = 0.8)` — keeps Info slightly stricter than today's 0.7, relaxes Warning/Critical so a source-verified Warning at 0.55-0.6 (the motivating incident) survives. Keep the values as named constants; they are judgment calls, configurable by callers.
- Replace `confidenceThreshold: Double = 0.7` in `reviewAndFixLoop`'s signature (ReviewLoop.scala:214) and in `ReviewLoopConfig` (ReviewLoop.scala:289) with `confidenceGate: ConfidenceGate = ConfidenceGate.default`. Breaking the parameter is fine: consumers are version-pinned scala-cli scripts, and no shipped flow (flows/*.sc) passes `confidenceThreshold`. Update the parameter scaladoc.
- Update tests: `flow/src/test/scala/orca/review/ReviewAndFixTest.scala` test "filters issues below the confidence threshold" (line 197) plus a new test showing severity-dependent admission (same confidence value admitted as Critical/Warning but dropped as Info). Test helpers `issue(...)` default to `Severity.Warning` — pass severity explicitly where it matters.
- README.md is the API reference and must stay accurate: update the `reviewAndFixLoop` row (~line 631, currently says "findings above the confidence threshold") and the issue-fields mention (~line 761).
- Do NOT touch the state-free `fixLoop` (ReviewLoop.scala:74) — it has no confidence filtering by design.

tasks.title: Record sub-threshold findings as ignored and report termination honestly
tasks.description:
Make gated-out findings visible instead of silently deleted, in flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/ReviewLoop.scala.

- Change `filterByConfidence` to return both kept and dropped issues (e.g. a small case class or tuple). Apply in both call sites in `runReviewersAndLint` (reviewer path ~line 420, lint path ~line 430) and thread the round's dropped issues up through `evaluate` to `run`'s loop.
- At every termination path of `ReviewFixLoop.run` — `LoopStep.Done`, `LoopStep.CapReached`, and the fixer-halt branch (`outcome.fixed.isEmpty`) — fold the FINAL round's dropped issues into the returned `IgnoredIssues` with a reason like `below confidence gate (Warning needs >= 0.6, reported 0.55)`. Use only the final round's dropped set: reviewer sessions persist across rounds (`ReviewLoopState.sessions`) and re-report the same sub-threshold finding every round, so accumulating per-round would duplicate entries; the final round's dropped set is exactly the still-open sub-threshold findings.
- Termination honesty: `LoopStep.Done` currently displays "No review comments" (ReviewLoop.scala:550). When the final round dropped findings, display instead something like "No issues above the confidence gate; N sub-threshold finding(s) recorded as ignored". Leave `fixLoop`'s identical string (line 87) alone — that loop has no filter.
- Update the now-stale comment at ReviewLoop.scala:494-496 ("confidence filter is applied before display so what's shown matches what the fixer receives") to the new story. Optionally show dropped findings in the per-reviewer Step body (ReviewFormatting.scala `formatReviewerOutcome`) annotated e.g. `(below gate)` — nice-to-have, keep simple if done.
- No extra plumbing is needed for the progress log / PR: `IgnoredIssues` is the stage result in flows (e.g. flows/issue-pr.sc:81-87) and `stage` (flow/src/main/scala/orca/Flow.scala) records the result JSON in the committed progress log.
- Tests in ReviewAndFixTest: (a) a sub-threshold finding lands in the returned IgnoredIssues with a below-gate reason; (b) a finding re-reported across multiple rounds appears exactly once; (c) the honest termination Step is emitted (capture events by passing a listener into `ReviewLoopFixture.control(new EventDispatcher(...))`).

tasks.title: Define the confidence contract in prompts and schema; de-anchor reviewers from the plan
tasks.description:
Give reviewers the contract they are being graded against, and license them to challenge the plan. Files: flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/ReviewIssue.scala, ReviewLoopPrompts.scala, and flow/src/main/resources/orca/review/prompts/{initial-review.md,re-review.md,summarise-lint.md}.

- ReviewIssue.scala: scaladoc for `confidence` — the reviewer's estimated probability that the finding is real and worth fixing, judged only on the evidence gathered (code read, behaviour traced); explicitly NOT deference to the plan, nor an estimate of whether the finding will be accepted.
- Machine channel: try Tapir's `@description` annotation (sttp.tapir.Schema.annotations.description) on the `confidence` field — `JsonData` derives a Tapir Schema and `JsonSchemaGen` (tools/src/main/scala/orca/util/JsonSchemaGen.scala) renders it into the schema every reviewer receives. Verify with an assertion in flow/src/test/scala/orca/review/JsonSchemaGenTest.scala that the rendered schema contains the description. If the derivation does not pick up the annotation, don't fight it — the prompt text below is the primary carrier.
- initial-review.md: add a short Confidence section: the definition above; severity measures impact while confidence measures certainty (orthogonal — a data-loss Warning verified in source deserves high confidence even if an Info about a missing test feels safer); and disclose the gate: findings below the per-severity minimums are not sent to the fixer this round but are recorded and reported as ignored. Render the ACTUAL gate values: extend `ReviewLoopPrompts.initialReview(task, diff)` to also take the `ConfidenceGate` and substitute its values via `PromptResource.render` placeholders; update the call site in `ReviewFixLoop.firstReview` (ReviewLoop.scala:377).
- De-anchoring clause (decision 6), also in initial-review.md: the task description and the plan behind it are context, not evidence — a decision made at planning time is as reviewable as the code implementing it; if a planned choice looks wrong, flag it at the confidence the evidence supports.
- re-review.md: one line noting the confidence contract from the initial prompt still applies. summarise-lint.md: replace "use reasonable confidence" with a pointer to the same definition (confidence = probability the lint finding is real and actionable).
- Test: render `initialReview` with the default gate and assert the gate values and the de-anchoring clause appear (a small munit test alongside the existing flow tests).

tasks.title: Harden the reviewer-selection prompt (prompt-only, no code triggers)
tasks.description:
Per the reporter's decision on improvement 4, do NOT add code-side content triggers (overfitting concern) — improve the picker's brief instead. File: flow/src/main/resources/orca/review/prompts/select-reviewers.md (loaded as `ReviewLoopPrompts.SelectReviewers`, used by `ReviewerSelector.agentDriven` in flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/ReviewerSelector.scala).

Rewrite the prompt to say, roughly: the picker runs with read-only repository access, so before excluding a reviewer it should look at what the change actually does (e.g. run `git diff`), not judge by the task title and file names alone; when uncertain whether a lens applies, include it — the cost of a needless review is small, the cost of a missed one is not; risk-bearing lenses (security, code-functionality) should be skipped only when the diff clearly contains nothing in their scope (e.g. a pure-documentation change with no executable code). Keep the existing instructions about copying names verbatim from `availableReviewers` and not returning an empty list when some reviewers apply.

Update `agentDriven`'s scaladoc in ReviewerSelector.scala if its description of the selection brief becomes stale. Note the existing safety net stays: the code already falls back to all eligible reviewers when the picker returns no usable names (ReviewerSelector.scala:158-167), and `files:` frontmatter pre-filters still apply. No new tests needed beyond the suite passing (the prompt is loaded eagerly, so a malformed resource fails existing tests).

resultJson.brief:
# Codebase briefing — Orca review-loop changes (issue #36)

Before writing or reviewing any Scala code, invoke the `direct-style-scala` skill (CLAUDE.md mandates this, including for subagents).

## Where the work lives
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/` — the whole review package: `ReviewLoop.scala` (the loop: `reviewAndFixLoop` entry at :189, `ReviewLoopConfig` at :282, `ReviewFixLoop` class with `filterByConfidence` at :331, `runReviewersAndLint` at :403, `evaluate` at :467, `run` at :527, shared `stopPolicy` at :49, state-free `fixLoop` at :74), `ReviewIssue.scala`, `IgnoredIssue.scala` (`IgnoredIssue(title, reason)` / `IgnoredIssues`), `ReviewResult.scala`, `FixOutcome.scala`, `Severity.scala` (Critical/Warning/Info), `ReviewerSelector.scala`, `Reviewers.scala`, `ReviewLoopPrompts.scala`, `ReviewFormatting.scala`.
- Prompt resources: `flow/src/main/resources/orca/review/prompts/` (`initial-review.md`, `re-review.md`, `fix.md`, `select-reviewers.md`, `summarise-lint.md`, `reviewers/*.md`). Loaded via `PromptResource.load` / rendered with `PromptResource.render(template, "key" -> value)` using `{{key}}` placeholders.
- Flows consuming the loop: `flows/issue-pr.sc` (and implement*.sc, simple.sc, issue-pr-bugfix.sc) — none passes `confidenceThreshold`, all rely on defaults.

## Capture checking (important)
`ReviewLoop.scala` and `ReviewerSelector.scala` start with `import language.experimental.captureChecking` + `separationChecking` and MUST keep compiling under CC. Tapir `derives`/macro types don't type-check under CC — anything with `derives JsonData` goes in a sibling non-CC file (that's why `ReviewIssue.scala`, `FixRequest.scala` etc. are separate). A plain case class with no derives (like the new `ConfidenceGate`) is fine either way. Do not delete the explicit type application at ReviewLoop.scala:436 or change `->` pure-arrow types — they are CC-load-bearing (comments in-file explain each).

## Loop mechanics you must not break
- Reviewers run in parallel via `CheckedPar.mapParUnordered`; per-reviewer results are confidence-filtered at ReviewLoop.scala:420 (reviewers) and :430 (lint) BEFORE display — the comment at :494 explains the current filter-before-display rationale and will need updating.
- Reviewer sessions persist across rounds (`ReviewLoopState.sessions`, resumed with `ReviewLoopPrompts.ReReview`), so a sub-threshold finding is typically RE-REPORTED every round — dedupe by folding only the FINAL round's dropped set into `IgnoredIssues` at termination, never accumulating per round.
- Three termination paths in `ReviewFixLoop.run` (and the shared `stopPolicy`): `Done` (prints "No review comments" at :550), `CapReached`, and fixer-halt (`outcome.fixed.isEmpty`). The state-free `fixLoop` (:74) shares `stopPolicy` and prints the same string at :87 but has NO confidence filter — leave it alone.
- `IgnoredIssues` returned by `reviewAndFixLoop` becomes the stage result in flows (`stage(...)` in `flow/src/main/scala/orca/Flow.scala` records the result JSON into the committed progress log), so folding dropped findings into it is all the plumbing needed for durable visibility. `IgnoredIssues` has a deliberately silent `Announce` given.
- `orca.display(msg)` emits a progress Step (no checkpoint); `ctx.emit(OrcaEvent.Step(...))` likewise from inside the loop.

## Schema / structured output
`JsonData` bundles a Tapir `Schema` + jsoniter codec; `JsonSchemaGen` (`tools/src/main/scala/orca/util/JsonSchemaGen.scala`) converts to OpenAI-strict JSON Schema that every reviewer backend receives, so a Tapir `@description` annotation on `ReviewIssue.confidence` (from `sttp.tapir.Schema.annotations`) is the machine-readable channel — verify it survives derivation + rendering via `JsonSchemaGenTest` before relying on it.

## Reviewer selection
`ReviewerSelector.agentDriven` pre-filters by `files:` frontmatter regexes (`ReviewerPrompts.filePatternsBySlug`; the shipped security reviewer has NO files: entry so it is always offered), asks a cheap read-only picker LLM with `select-reviewers.md` + task title + changed file names, post-filters hallucinated names, and already falls back to all eligible reviewers if the picker returns nothing usable (ReviewerSelector.scala:158-167). The picker agent runs `withReadOnly` in the flow workdir, so it CAN inspect the diff if the prompt tells it to.

## Conventions & verification
- Scala 3 braceless syntax, explicit return types on public members, zero-warning compile, munit for tests. Format with `sbt scalafmtAll` before committing.
- Tests: `sbt "flow/test"`; single suite: `sbt "flow/testOnly orca.review.ReviewAndFixTest"`. Fixtures: `FakeAgent`/`FakeAgentCall`/`TokenEmittingReviewer` and `ReviewLoopFixture.control(new EventDispatcher(listeners))` in `flow/src/test/scala/orca/review/` — pass an `OrcaListener` to capture emitted Steps for display assertions. Loop tests mint `given orca.InStage = orca.InStage.unsafe` and `given orca.WorkspaceWrite = orca.WorkspaceWrite.unsafe`, use `reviewerSelection = ReviewerSelector.allEveryRound` and `initialDiff = Some("")` to avoid git.
- README.md doubles as the API reference (keep its tables accurate — `reviewAndFixLoop` row ~line 631, issue-fields note ~line 761). Consumers are version-pinned scala-cli scripts: breaking `reviewAndFixLoop`'s signature is acceptable and expected here.
- Default gate values agreed in planning (judgment call, keep configurable): Critical ≥ 0.5, Warning ≥ 0.6, Info ≥ 0.8 (old flat default was 0.7).
- sbt runs take a while — run long test commands in the background and one implementer at a time.
